record.paper_title: Variational principles in grid generation and geometric modelling: theoretical justifications and open problems
record.original_question: Given a mapping whose total metric distortion is below a threshold 1/t in the quasi-isometric condition det grad y > t Phi(det grad y, grad y), can one construct a convergent sequence of piecewise-affine approximations such that every approximation also stays below the same distortion threshold 1/t, and can this construction be made practical?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega, \Omega^* \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ be bounded domains and let $y : \Omega 	o \Omega^*$ be a smooth orientation-preserving diffeomorphism. For a fixed parameter $t > 1$, define the pointwise quasi-isometric distortion functional through a polyconvex density $\Phi(\det 
abla y, 
abla y)$ (for instance $\Phi(J,F) = 	frac{1}{2}(\|F\|^2/J + J)$ in the planar case, or its $n$-dimensional analogue built from principal invariants of $(
abla y)^	op 
abla y$), and assume that the mapping $y$ satisfies the quasi-isometric condition
$$ \det 
abla y(x) \; > \; t \, \Phi(\det 
abla y(x), 
abla y(x)) \qquad 	ext{for almost every } x \in \Omega, $$
so that the total metric distortion of $y$ is strictly below the threshold $1/t$.

Question: Does there exist a sequence $\{y_h\}_{h>0}$ of continuous piecewise-affine mappings, defined on a family of simplicial triangulations of $\Omega$ with mesh size $h 	o 0$, such that:
(i) $y_h 	o y$ (in a suitable Sobolev sense, e.g. $W^{1,p}(\Omega)$ for appropriate $p$);
(ii) each $y_h$ satisfies the same quasi-isometric bound, i.e.\ $\det 
abla y_h > t\,\Phi(\det 
abla y_h, 
abla y_h)$ on every simplex; and
(iii) the construction of $\{y_h\}$ can be carried out by an effective (practically implementable) algorithm?
artifact.status_search_result: Recent work on "lowest distortion mappings" and "practical lowest distortion mapping" (Garanzha et al., 2022) reports algorithmic, variational constructions of piecewise-affine quasi-isometric mappings whose distortion can be controlled and which converge to a target quasi-isometric map. These developments provide practical algorithms that achieve distortion equidistribution, indicating partial progress toward the construction, though a complete theoretical proof that the discrete approximations preserve the exact same distortion threshold 1/t for arbitrary admissible $y$ does not appear to be fully established in the literature.

status_evidence.title: Lowest distortion mappings and equidistribution principle
status_evidence.snippet: Variational method that can provably construct 3D quasi-isometric mappings between domains of complex shape; polyconvex distortion measures with local maximum principle controlling invertibility and distortion bounds.
status_evidence.claim: Provides variational constructions of piecewise-affine quasi-isometric maps with controlled discrete distortion.

status_evidence.title: Practical lowest distortion mapping
status_evidence.snippet: Physics-based quasi-isometric stiffening algorithm for max-norm minimization of hyperelastic distortion; equidistributes distortion over the domain.
status_evidence.claim: Demonstrates a practical algorithm producing piecewise-affine approximations with controlled distortion.

status_evidence.title: In the Quest for Scale-optimal Mappings
status_evidence.snippet: Algorithmic framework for distortion-minimizing piecewise-affine maps.
status_evidence.claim: Indicates ongoing partial progress on practical constructions.
